stats.title: Global Birth Statistics: A Living History

speed.title: The Speed of Human Birth
speed.description: According to the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA), approximately 140 million babies are born every year worldwide. That translates to roughly 4.25 births per second, 255 births per minute, and 15,300 births per hour. The global population has grown from approximately 2.5 billion in 1950 to over 8.35 billion in 2026.

growth.title: Population Growth Trends
growth.description: The peak of global population growth occurred in the 1960s at nearly 2.1% per year. Today's growth rate has slowed to approximately 0.9% annually, with projections suggesting the global population will peak around 10.4 billion in the 2080s.

personal.title: Your Personal Connection to Global Population
personal.description: When you enter your birthdate on UniversePulse, you'll discover the number of people who have been born during your lifetime — a number that puts your existence into a fascinating global context. For most people, this number falls between 1 billion and 5 billion.

items.q: How many people are born each day?
items.a: Approximately 380,000 people are born each day worldwide, according to UN DESA estimates.

items.q: When did the global population reach 8 billion?
items.a: The United Nations declared that the global population reached 8 billion on November 15, 2022.

items.q: What is the world population in 2026?
items.a: As of 2026, the world population is estimated to be approximately 8.35 billion people.
UniversePulse uses a simple but accurate mathematical model based on authoritative data from UN DESA, the World Bank, and other demographic sources.

hero.title: How Much CO₂ Have I Emitted Since I Was Born?
hero.description: Every second, humanity releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere at an alarming rate. See the total CO₂ emissions that have occurred since the day you were born.

cta.title: Calculate Your Carbon Lifetime
cta.description: Enter your birthdate to discover the total CO₂ emissions that have accumulated during your lifetime — a number that puts your existence into a planetary context.

emissions.title: The Scale of Global Emissions
emissions.description: Annual global CO₂ emissions from fossil fuels have exceeded 36 billion tonnes in recent years. This is approximately 4.7 tonnes per person per year on average, though emissions vary dramatically between developed and developing nations.

targets.title: Climate Targets and Reality
targets.description: To limit global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels, the remaining carbon budget is estimated at around 250 gigatonnes of CO₂ — roughly 6 more years of current emissions. The Paris Agreement committed nations to drastically reduce emissions by 2030.

items.q: What is the main source of CO₂ emissions?
items.a: Burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, and natural gas) for energy, transportation, and industry accounts for the vast majority of global CO₂ emissions.

items.q: How much CO₂ does the average person emit?
items.a: The global average per capita CO₂ emission is approximately 4.7 tonnes per year, though this varies from under 1 tonne in some developing nations to over 15 tonnes in the most developed countries.

items.q: What is the carbon budget for 1.5°C?
items.a: The remaining carbon budget to keep warming below 1.5°C is estimated at around 250 gigatonnes of CO₂ — roughly 6 more years at current emission rates.

UniversePulse uses a mathematical model based on authoritative data from the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the Global Carbon Project, applying the current global emission rate since your birthdate.

hero.title: How Far Has Earth Traveled Since I Was Born?
hero.description: Our planet is in constant motion — orbiting the Sun at 107,000 km/h, while the entire solar system travels through the Milky Way at 828,000 km/h. See the incredible cosmic distance covered since your birth.

cta.title: Calculate Your Cosmic Journey
cta.description: Enter your birthdate to discover the total distance Earth has traveled through space during your lifetime — a number that puts your existence into a cosmic perspective.

cosmos.title: Earth's Cosmic Journey
cosmos.description: Earth orbits the Sun at an average speed of 107,000 km/h, completing one orbit every 365.25 days. Meanwhile, our entire solar system travels around the center of the Milky Way galaxy at approximately 828,000 km/h. Since you were born, Earth has traveled a distance that is almost incomprehensible.

items.q: How fast does Earth orbit the Sun?
items.a: Earth travels at approximately 107,000 km/h (67,000 mph) in its orbit around the Sun.

items.q: How far does Earth travel in one year?
items.a: Earth travels approximately 940 million kilometers (584 million miles) in one complete orbit around the Sun.
Earth's orbital speed varies slightly throughout the year due to the elliptical shape of its orbit — fastest at perihelion (closest to Sun) and slowest at aphelion (farthest from Sun).
UniversePulse uses a precise mathematical model based on Earth's orbital parameters from NASA, calculating the total distance traveled since your birthdate.

science.title: The Science of Sea Level Rise

causes.title: Causes of Sea Level Rise
causes.description: Sea level rise is driven primarily by thermal expansion of warming ocean water and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets). Since 1993, global sea level has risen at an accelerating rate of approximately 3.6 mm per year.

projections.title: Future Projections
projections.description: The IPCC projects sea levels could rise by 0.3 to 1.1 meters by 2100, depending on emissions scenarios. Even the most optimistic scenarios imply continued rise for centuries due to the thermal inertia of the oceans.

items.q: How much has sea level risen since 1900?
items.a: Global average sea level has risen by approximately 21-24 cm (8-10 inches) since 1900, with the rate accelerating in recent decades.

items.q: What is the current rate of sea level rise?
items.a: The current rate is approximately 3.6 mm per year, and it is accelerating. In some regions, the rate is even higher due to local factors.

items.q: How does sea level rise affect coastal cities?
items.a: Rising seas threaten coastal communities through increased flooding, storm surge intensity, saltwater intrusion into freshwater, and erosion of shorelines. Over 1 billion people live in low-lying coastal zones.

items.q: How does UniversePulse calculate sea level rise?
items.a: UniversePulse uses a mathematical model based on IPCC data and satellite observations, estimating cumulative sea level rise since your birthdate.

privacy.description: How UniversePulse collects and uses your data.
privacy.contact: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at

sections.heading: 1. Information We Collect
sections.content: UniversePulse does not collect, store, or sell any personal data. We do not use cookies for tracking, nor do we maintain user accounts. The only data we process is the birth date you voluntarily enter into the birthday calculator, which is processed entirely in your browser and never transmitted to our servers.

sections.heading: 2. How We Use Information
sections.content: Since we do not collect personal data, we do not use or process any information about you. The birth date you enter is used locally in your browser to calculate personal statistics. This data is not sent to any third party.

sections.heading: 3. Google Analytics
sections.content: We use Google Analytics (gtag.js) to understand how visitors interact with our site. Google Analytics collects standard internet log information and visitor behavior information in an anonymous, aggregated form. It does not identify individual users. Google's privacy policy applies to the data collected by its analytics services.

sections.heading: 4. Data Security
sections.content: Since we do not collect personal data, there is no personal data to secure. All calculations happen client-side in your browser. We use HTTPS to protect the connection between your browser and our servers.

sections.heading: 5. Third-Party Services
sections.content: We use Google Analytics for site analytics. By using our site, you consent to the collection and use of information by Google Analytics as described in their privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

sections.heading: 6. Children's Privacy
sections.content: UniversePulse is not intended for children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you are a parent and believe your child has provided us with personal information, please contact us.

sections.heading: 7. Changes to This Policy
sections.content: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page and updating the "Last updated" date.

sections.heading: 8. Contact Us
sections.content: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please contact us at support@universepulse.net.

about.title: About UniversePulse
about.description: Our mission to make global data personal and accessible.
about.intro: UniversePulse is a real-time global data dashboard that transforms abstract macro-level statistics into deeply personal, emotionally resonant experiences. We believe that understanding global population, resource consumption, and environmental change should be accessible, beautiful, and meaningful to every individual.
about.mission: Our mission is to help every person on Earth understand their place in the global system — not as a passive observer, but as an active participant in the ongoing story of humanity and our planet. When you enter your birth date, you discover that the numbers behind global change are also your numbers.
about.data: All data on UniversePulse comes from authoritative annual sources including the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA), the International Energy Agency (IEA), BP Statistical Review, FAO, and the Global Carbon Project. Annual totals are converted to per-second average rates using mathematical models. These are estimates for educational display, not precise measurements.
about.team: UniversePulse is an independent project built with Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. We are a small team passionate about data visualization, climate awareness, and making complex global statistics accessible to everyone.
about.contact: We would love to hear from you. Reach us at
